reply.rationale: No defensible multi-entry compositional paradigm is supported by the supplied codebook. Although some symbols share characters with standalone entries (e.g. T, B, C, W, F, R, O, 6, 2E, 4C), the longer codes do not form meaning-consistent substitution frames whose whole meanings are predictable from reusable parts. For example, TB is not compositionally 'top face + bell', CD is not predictably 'cool cloth + drape cloth', and symbols like PI, LO, WB, BF, CV, PE, WH behave as opaque labels rather than products of a shared construction. There is also no confirmed alternating frame showing stable morpheme contributions across multiple segmented entries. Per the instructions, a flat lexicon is preferred over unsupported morphology.
